Project fit

Transform Your Existing Deck With Thoughtful Design and Remodeling

A worn or dated deck can limit how much you enjoy your yard. RT Signature Homes reworks the structure, surfaces, railings, and layout together, so your remodeled deck is safe, low-maintenance, and ready for relaxing and entertaining outdoors.

Typical scope

  • Footings, framing, ledger, and flashing assessment
  • Composite, hardwood, or pressure-treated decking
  • Railings, stairs, lighting, and privacy screening
  • Waterproofing, drainage, and under-deck details
  • Permits, inspections, and structural coordination

Why choose us

Why Choose Us for Your Deck Remodeling Project

Structure before surface

A deck remodeling project is only as sound as its framing, so we evaluate footings, posts, and ledger connections before choosing a decking material.

Detailed for the weather

Pacific Northwest decks live under rain and shade, so drainage, ventilation, and flashing are planned to protect both the deck and the house it attaches to.

Built for how you use it

Railings, stairs, lighting, and covered areas are designed around how the outdoor space will actually be used across the seasons.

Design ideas

Replace Worn Decking Materials With Durable and Attractive Finishes

Faded boards, splinters, and warping are usually the first signs a deck needs new surfaces. Replacing worn decking with durable, attractive materials refreshes the whole space and cuts down on upkeep.

Deck & Outdoor Living Ideas

Explore composite, cedar, and pressure-treated decking, along with railing, stair, and lighting options chosen to suit Pacific Northwest weather and the way you use your deck.

Explore the gallery

Layout & comfort

Improve Outdoor Comfort With Better Deck Layout and Planning

A comfortable deck starts with a layout planned around how you want to use it, with defined areas for seating, dining, grilling, and easy movement between them.

We consider sun and shade, sightlines, privacy, and access from the house, so the space feels inviting throughout the day and connects naturally to your indoor living areas.

Thoughtful planning of levels, steps, and built-in features makes the deck more usable for everyday relaxing and for entertaining groups of guests.

Railings & finishes

Upgrade Deck Railings for Improved Safety and Visual Appeal

Railings are both a safety requirement and one of the most visible design elements of a deck, so upgrading them improves protection and appearance at once.

Options such as cable, aluminum, glass, and wood railings are selected for code-compliant height and spacing while opening up views and complementing your home's exterior.

Pairing updated railings with new lighting, stairs, and finishes gives the deck a cohesive, finished look that lasts through changing seasons.

How the work moves

A process that keeps decisions ahead of construction.

Discovery and site assessment

We clarify goals, review existing conditions, identify constraints, and determine what needs deeper investigation before a scope is written.

Design and pre-construction

Layout, materials, trade requirements, permits, allowances, schedule factors, and decision deadlines are coordinated into one buildable plan.

Construction and completion

The work is sequenced, protected, inspected, communicated, and closed out with a final walkthrough and documented completion items.

Budget and schedule orientation

Scope the variables before suggesting a number.

Useful early guidance identifies what changes the investment and timeline. A responsible project range follows an assessment of the property, scope, finish expectations, and delivery constraints.

Common factors

  • Existing structural and mechanical conditions
  • Project size, layout changes, and finish level
  • Permit, engineering, and design requirements
  • Material availability and product lead times
  • Site access, protection, and project sequencing

Questions homeowners ask

Deck Remodeling FAQs

How do I know whether my deck needs remodeling or complete replacement?

A deck with faded finishes, outdated railings, or worn boards may only need targeted remodeling. However, widespread wood rot, unstable supports, loose connections, or significant structural damage may require repairs or partial or complete replacement. A proper inspection helps determine the safest and most practical approach.

Can I change the shape or size of my existing deck?

Yes, deck remodeling may include expanding the platform, adjusting its shape, or reconfiguring access points. The feasibility depends on the existing structure, available space, property conditions, and applicable building requirements. Structural changes should be evaluated before construction begins.

Which deck materials are suitable for an outdoor space exposed to changing weather?

Pressure-treated wood, naturally durable wood species, and composite decking are common options. Each has different maintenance requirements, costs, and appearance. Your choice should account for moisture exposure, sunlight, expected foot traffic, and how much ongoing maintenance you prefer.

Can deck remodeling make my outdoor space more useful for entertaining guests?

Yes, a better layout can create dedicated areas for seating, dining, grilling, and movement. Features such as built-in benches, wider steps, updated railings, and outdoor lighting may improve usability, provided the deck has enough space and the design accommodates safety requirements.

What should be checked before installing new decking over an existing structure?

The underlying frame, joists, support posts, connections, drainage, and signs of rot or insect damage should be inspected first. New boards cannot correct an unsafe structure. Any necessary repairs and ventilation or moisture concerns should be addressed before new decking is installed.
